facts.advisory_summary:
bytes has integer overflow in BytesMut::reserve — # Details

In the unique reclaim path of `BytesMut::reserve`, the condition
```rs
if v_capacity >= new_cap + offset
```
uses an unchecked addition. When `new_cap + offset` overflows `usize` in release builds, this condition may incorrectly pass, causing `self.cap` to be set to a value that exceeds the actual allocated capacity. Subsequent APIs such as `spare_capacity_mut()` then trust this corrupted `cap` value and may create out-of-bounds slices, leading to UB.

This behavior is observable in release builds (integer overflow wraps), whereas de

expect.note: bytes 1.8.0 BytesMut::reserve unique-reclaim overflow needs new_cap+offset to wrap usize (additional ~2^64). All reserve callers on the request paths size from in-memory/bounded lengths (hyper h1 role.rs:410/io.rs:266, h2 hpack huffman/mod.rs:24 src.len()<<1, tungstenite frame/mod.rs:221 frame.len(), tokio-util length_delimited saturating_sub); no caller passes an attacker-chosen near-usize::MAX value. The function runs constantly, but the overflow condition cannot be met.

facts.advisory_summary: Diesel's SQLite backend has possible UTF-8 corruption — Diesel uses the `sqlite3_value_text` function to receive strings from SQLite while deserializing query results. We misinterpreted the corresponding [SQLite](https://sqlite.org/c3ref/value_blob.html) documentation that this function always returns a UTF-8 encoded string values as `*const c_char`. Based on that we used `str::from_utf8_unchecked` to construct a Rust string slice without any additional UTF-8 checks in place. It turned out that this function doesn't always return correct UTF-8 strings. For field of the SQLite side storage type

expect.note: SQLite is the image's default backend and SqliteValue::read_str runs on every Text column read. The UB needs a non-UTF-8 TEXT value in the DB, but the app writes only Rust Strings via bound Text params (always valid UTF-8). Blob columns (sends.password_hash/salt, users password_hash/salt) are typed Binary in src/db/schemas/sqlite/schema.rs:142-143,200-201, so read_str is never called on blobs. Attacker data cannot produce invalid UTF-8 in a Text column.

facts.advisory_summary:
`event-listener` allows `!Send` tags to cross thread boundaries via `StackSlot` — Affected versions of `event-listener` unconditionally implement `Send` and
`Sync` for `StackSlot<'_, T>`, the stack-allocated listener type created
by the `listener!` macro.

This allows a `!Send` tag type set via `Event::with_tag` to be moved to

expect.note: event-listener 5.3.1 comes in only through async-lock/async-process/event-listener-strategy/async-channel, all under async-std. async-std is pulled in only by lettre's optional async-std1 feature (lettre Cargo.toml:186-188, appearing in the lock through the weak 'async-std?/unstable' in sendmail-transport). facts.advisory_summary:
h2 unbounded empty DATA frames — The h2 crate, used internally by hyper, had a flaw that would accept and queue empty DATA frames without limit.
If streams were not actively drained, this could lead to unbounded memory usage, or a panic if the length overflows.

Low severity.

Patched in v0.4.16.

expect.note: h2 0.3.26 is used by hyper 0.14.31, which is Rocket's HTTP server (rocket_http). Rocket is built without http2, but reqwest 0.11 (via yubico) turns on hyper 0.14 'http2' (reqwest-0.11.27 Cargo.toml:271-279). With http1+http2 both compiled, hyper's server ConnectionMode::default() is Fallback (hyper server/conn.rs:972-976), so the internet-facing port 80 Rocket server (rocket server.rs:509) accepts h2c prior-knowledge connections. An unauthenticated client can stream empty DATA frames to the h2 server. Inferred from feature unification.

facts.advisory_summary:

The name compression logic then searches for matches with a linear scan.

A malicious message with many records can both introduce many candidate labels,
and invoke this linear scan many times. This can amplify CPU exhaustion in DoS
attacks.

This is similar to
[CVE-2024-8508](https://www.nlnetlabs.nl/downloads/unbound/CVE-2024-8508.txt).

We recommend all affected users up

expect.note: BinEncoder name compression is O(n^2) in the number of records being encoded. As a stub resolver, vaultwarden only encodes outgoing single-question queries. Received responses are decoded, not re-encoded; DnsResponse::from_message (dns_response.rs:147-149, which calls to_vec) is called only from tests (lookup.rs:576, caching_client.rs:628, retry_dns_handle.rs:174). facts.advisory_summary: hickory-resolver: Resolver::lookup() and Resolver::lookup_ip() APIs obscure DNSSEC validation failures — When calling `Resolver::lookup()` or `Resolver::lookup_ip()` on a resolver with DNSSEC validation enabled, both methods return `Ok(...)` if DNSSEC validation fails. It is possible but very inconvenient to check the validation status of individual records. These methods should instead return an error when DNSSEC validation determines a response is bogus.

expect.note: The advisory applies only when the resolver has DNSSEC validation enabled. hickory dnssec features are not compiled (no ring/openssl deps of hickory-proto in Cargo.lock), and ResolverOpts come from read_system_conf (http_client.rs:186-190), which has validate=false.

Vaultwarden's icon Jar is CookieStore::default() (icons.rs:621-623, #[derive(Default)]) with public_suffix_list None, so idna 0.3 code never runs. url uses idna 1.0.3.

facts.advisory_summary:
`idna` accepts Punycode labels that do not produce any non-ASCII when decoded — `idna` 0.5.0 and earlier accepts Punycode labels that do not produce any non-ASCII output, which means that either ASCII labels or the empty root label can be masked such that they appear unequal without IDNA processing or when processed with a different implementation and equal when processed with `idna` 0.5.0 or earlier.

facts.advisory_summary:
jsonwebtoken has Type Confusion that leads to potential authorization bypass — ## Summary:

It has been discovered that there is a Type Confusion vulnerability in jsonwebtoken, specifically, in its claim validation logic.

When a standard claim (such as nbf or exp) is provided with an incorrect JSON type (Like a String instead of a Number), the library’s internal parsing mechanism marks the claim as “FailedToParse”. Crucially, the validation logic treats this “FailedToParse” state identically to “NotPresent”.

This means that if a check is enabled (like: validate_nbf = true), but the claim is

expect.note: jsonwebtoken::decode (auth.rs:97) runs on attacker tokens with validate_nbf/exp. The type-confusion bypass needs a token whose signature verifies but whose nbf/exp has the wrong JSON type. Tokens are RS256-signed with the server's private key (auth.rs:83, 90), and signatures are checked before claims, so an attacker cannot mint such a token. Claims also deserialize into i64 nbf/exp fields (auth.rs:147-149), which would fail anyway.

rust-openssl has incorrect bounds assertion in aes key wrap — ### Summary
``aes::unwrap_key()`` has an incorrect bounds assertion on the out buffer size, which can lead to out-of-bounds write.

### Details
``aes::unwrap_key()`` contains an incorrect assertion: it checks that `out.len() + 8 <= in_.len()`, but this condition is reversed. The intended invariant is `out.len() >= in_.len() - 8`, ensuring the output buffer is large enough.

Because of the inverted check, the function only accepts buffers at or below the minimum required size and rejects larger ones. If a smaller buffer is provided t

expect.note: openssl::aes::unwrap_key (aes.rs:235) is not called by vaultwarden (only Rsa in auth.rs:7, 53-58), native-tls 0.2.12 or webauthn-rs 0.3.2 (grep). The Debian bookworm image also links OpenSSL 3.

facts.advisory_summary: rust-openssl: rustMdCtxRef::digest_final() writes past caller buffer with no length check — `EVP_DigestFinal()` always writes `EVP_MD_CTX_size(ctx)` to the `out` buffer. If `out` is smaller than that, `MdCtxRef::digest_final()` writes past its end, usually corrupting the stack. This is reachable from safe Rust.

expect.note: MdCtxRef::digest_final (md_ctx.rs:242) is not called by vaultwarden, native-tls or webauthn-rs (webauthn uses openssl::hash/sign/x509). The only callers are md_ctx tests.

facts.advisory_summary: rust-openssl: Unchecked callback length in PSK/cookie trampolines leaks adjacent memory to peer — The FFI trampolines behind `SslContextBuilder::set_psk_client_callback`, `set_psk_server_callback`, `set_cookie_generate_cb`,  and `set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb` forwarded the user closure's returned usize directly to OpenSSL without checking it against the `&mut [u8]` that was handed to the closure. This can lead to buffer overflows and other unintended consequences.

expect.note: set_psk_*_callback / set_cookie_generate_cb / set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb are not used by native-tls (imp/openssl.rs), webauthn-rs or vaultwarden. No PSK or DTLS cookies.

facts.advisory_summary:
rust-openssl: Potential out-of-bounds write in `CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_inplace` for AES-KW-PAD ciphers — `CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_inplace` incorrectly sized output buffers when used with AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers (EVP_aes_{128,192,256}_wrap_pad). For a non-multiple-of-8 input, OpenSSL writes up to 7 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer or Vec, producing attacker-controllable heap corruption when the plaintext length is attacker-influenced.

This only impacts users using AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers.

This method was missed in the fix for GHSA-xv59-967r-8726

expect.note: No AES key-wrap-with-padding cipher (aes_*_wrap_pad) or CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_inplace use in vaultwarden, native-tls or webauthn-rs (grep symm/cipher_ctx/wrap_pad finds nothing).

facts.advisory_summary: rust-openssl: Deriver::derive and PkeyCtxRef::derive can overflow short buffers on OpenSSL 1.1.1 — `Deriver::derive` (and `PkeyCtxRef::derive`) sets `len = buf.len()` and passes it as the in/out length to `EVP_PKEY_derive`, relying on OpenSSL to honor it. On OpenSSL 1.1.x, X25519, X448, DH and HKDF-extract  ignore the incoming `*keylen`, unconditionally writing the full shared secret (32/56/prime-size bytes). A caller passing a short slice gets a heap/stack overflow from safe code. OpenSSL 3.x providers do check, so this only impacts older OpenSSL.

expect.note: Deriver::derive/PkeyCtxRef::derive are not called by vaultwarden, native-tls or webauthn-rs. The issue also only affects OpenSSL 1.1.x, and the image is debian:bookworm-slim (OpenSSL 3, Dockerfile.debian). The ring::pbkdf2::derive in crypto.rs:16 is unrelated.

facts.advisory_summary: rust-opennssl has an Out-of-bounds read in PEM password callback when returning an oversized length — The `*_from_pem_callback` APIs did not validate the length returned by the user's callback. A password callback that returns a value larger than the buffer it was given can cause some versions of OpenSSL to over-read this buffer. OpenSSL 3.x is not affected by this.

expect.note: No *_from_pem_callback use: auth.rs:53 uses Rsa::private_key_from_pem (no callback) on the server's own key file. Only OpenSSL < 3 is affected anyway, and the bookworm image has OpenSSL 3.

facts.advisory_summary: rust-openssl has undefined behavior in X509Ref::ocsp_responders for certificates with non-UTF-8 OCSP URLs — `X509Ref::ocsp_responders` returns OCSP responder URLs from a certificate's AIA extension as `OpensslString`, whose `Deref<Target = str>` wraps the raw bytes with `str::from_utf8_unchecked`. OpenSSL does not enforce that the underlying IA5String is ASCII, so a certificate with non-UTF-8 bytes in its OCSP accessLocation causes safe Rust code to construct a `&str` that violates the UTF-8 invariant — resulting in undefined behavior.

expect.note: X509Ref::ocsp_responders (x509/mod.rs:604) is not called by vaultwarden, native-tls or webauthn-rs (grep).

facts.advisory_summary:
rust-openssl vulnerable to heap buffer overflow when encrypting with AES key-wrap-with-padding — `CipherCtxRef::cipher_update`, `CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_vec`, and `symm::Crypter::update` incorrectly sized output buffers when used with AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers (`EVP_aes_{128,192,256}_wrap_pad`). facts.advisory_summary:
Unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange — The client recorded the server-selected key exchange group for each server

This record is used to predict which key share to send in future ClientHellos
